passage: I'm Ayesha, at the next desk in the design team. For weeks Kavitha had looked worn out. Then on Thursday at the tea point I saw her and Rohit talking in low voices. Rohit was showing her notes on his phone; then she showed him hers. I caught "dates", "same words" and "same here", and by the end her shoulders had come down and she laughed once. When I asked later, Kavitha only said, "Facts, not gossip." She told Rohit not to do anything on her account, and he agreed they would only go to HR if both wanted to. I can't say exactly what she feels, and I don't know the whole story, but she looks lighter than she has in a month.

qa.q: Where did Ayesha see Kavitha and Rohit talking?
qa.a: Ayesha saw them at the tea point on Thursday.

qa.q: What might Kavitha have felt as she compared notes with Rohit?
qa.a: She may have felt relief that it was not just her, since her shoulders came down and she laughed once, though Ayesha admits she cannot say exactly.

qa.q: How can two colleagues support each other in a situation like this?
qa.a: They can share facts and dates rather than gossip, and support each other without pulling anyone into a risky move, as Kavitha and Rohit agreed.

qa.q: How might Rohit have felt while sharing notes?
qa.a: Rohit may also have felt relief at finding he was not alone, since Ayesha heard "same here" and Rohit agreed to go to HR only if both wanted to.

grounding: A coworker admits facing the same treatment and Kavitha and Rohit quietly compare facts, feeling relief without a risky move.
